investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes advertising the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was collected (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), confirming the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but reported it as exhausted ("Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"); the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-carrying nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing the expected-output contract to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=135433, pod stuck unscheduled for 129s before the check ended.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was written, confirming the agent pod never reached a schedulable state.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, satisfying zero of the two contract assertions (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]).

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=150947, empty evidenceKeys — same scheduling failure reproduced a third time.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract at line 256 requires vmIdPresent and remoteState, both of which depend on a successfully scheduled and running VM pod.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the two peerpods-capable nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to the two peerpods nodes, but if those rules were recently tightened or the node labels changed, the effective eligible set could have shrunk, making exhaustion more likely.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the production cluster has only 2 nodes capable of hosting kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads; if demand increased or nodes were cordoned/drained, capacity could be transiently or persistently exhausted.

Lower probability — eval runner token or org configuration issue: the runner does check for a missing token at line 1882 (source-context run-status-probes.mjs:1876-1884) and would return SKIP rather than fail with a scheduler message, so this is ruled out as the primary cause for this specific failure message.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of the eval that returns vmIdPresent=true and a valid remoteState would indicate the scheduling failure was transient and capacity has recovered.

Cluster node inspection showing kata.peerpods.io/vm resources are not exhausted (i.e., allocatable > allocated on the two eligible nodes) would suggest the root cause is a pod spec misconfiguration (wrong resource request quantity or wrong node selector) rather than capacity exhaustion.

Evidence that the two peerpods-capable nodes were cordoned, drained, or had their kata.peerpods.io/vm label removed at the time of the eval run would shift the cause from exhaustion to node availability.

A passing result on remote-agent-create while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime still fail would indicate the failures are not fully shared and the root cause may be more nuanced than a single capacity constraint.

Confirmation that no other workloads were consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the failure would suggest the resource quantity advertised by the nodes is too low (provisioning misconfiguration) rather than runtime exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, so capacity exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure signal rather than a pod scheduling timeout.

Add an eval that verifies the number of peerpods-capable nodes (nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource) meets a minimum threshold, alerting if the eligible node count drops below the expected value.

Add a latency-banded eval for remote agent pod scheduling time specifically, distinct from the full agent creation eval, so scheduling delays can be detected and alerted before they cause full timeouts.

Consider adding a sibling eval that checks for Unschedulable events in the cluster's event stream for the remote-agents namespace, enabling earlier detection of scheduling pressure before the full outageLatencyMs threshold is crossed.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-27T07:32–07:37Z with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and 4 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, preventing any remote agent pod from being scheduled. Because no agent pod could be created, the eval runner never reached the state-polling step, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are absent from the check result.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) is exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. The scheduler reports "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and confirms preemption cannot help. This prevented the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) from producing a schedulable pod, so the probe timed out after ~143 s without ever writing the required evidence fields orgId, agentId, readyState, or state, causing the remote-agent-state contract validation to fail entirely.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: existing remote agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for new probe pods. Preemption is explicitly ruled out by the scheduler message.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. If the affinity configuration changed or nodes were drained/replaced, the effective capacity could have dropped to zero.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning or node failure: one or both of the 2 affinity-matching nodes may have been cordoned, drained, or lost, reducing kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the minimum needed to schedule a new probe pod.

QUATERNARY — Leaked or stuck remote agent pods from prior eval runs consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903), progressively exhausting capacity across runs.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes advertising the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was collected (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), confirming the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but reported it as exhausted ("Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"); the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-carrying nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing the expected-output contract to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=135433, pod stuck unscheduled for 129s before the check ended.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was written, confirming the agent pod never reached a schedulable state.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, satisfying zero of the two contract assertions (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]).
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=151072, empty evidenceKeys — same scheduling failure reproduced independently.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=150947, empty evidenceKeys — same scheduling failure reproduced a third time.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which must succeed before any evidence can be written; the scheduler rejection prevents this call from completing.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract at line 256 requires vmIdPresent and remoteState, both of which depend on a successfully scheduled and running VM pod.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the two peerpods-capable nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to the two peerpods nodes, but if those rules were recently tightened or the node labels changed, the effective eligible set could have shrunk, making exhaustion more likely.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the production cluster has only 2 nodes capable of hosting kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads; if demand increased or nodes were cordoned/drained, capacity could be transiently or persistently exhausted.

Lower probability — eval runner token or org configuration issue: the runner does check for a missing token at line 1882 (source-context run-status-probes.mjs:1876-1884) and would return SKIP rather than fail with a scheduler message, so this is ruled out as the primary cause for this specific failure message.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of the eval that returns vmIdPresent=true and a valid remoteState would indicate the scheduling failure was transient and capacity has recovered.

Cluster node inspection showing kata.peerpods.io/vm resources are not exhausted (i.e., allocatable > allocated on the two eligible nodes) would suggest the root cause is a pod spec misconfiguration (wrong resource request quantity or wrong node selector) rather than capacity exhaustion.

Evidence that the two peerpods-capable nodes were cordoned, drained, or had their kata.peerpods.io/vm label removed at the time of the eval run would shift the cause from exhaustion to node availability.

A passing result on remote-agent-create while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime still fail would indicate the failures are not fully shared and the root cause may be more nuanced than a single capacity constraint.

Confirmation that no other workloads were consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the failure would suggest the resource quantity advertised by the nodes is too low (provisioning misconfiguration) rather than runtime exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, so capacity exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure signal rather than a pod scheduling timeout.

Add an eval that verifies the number of peerpods-capable nodes (nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource) meets a minimum threshold, alerting if the eligible node count drops below the expected value.

Add a latency-banded eval for remote agent pod scheduling time specifically, distinct from the full agent creation eval, so scheduling delays can be detected and alerted before they cause full timeouts.

Consider adding a sibling eval that checks for Unschedulable events in the cluster's event stream for the remote-agents namespace, enabling earlier detection of scheduling pressure before the full outageLatencyMs threshold is crossed.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-27T07:32–07:37Z with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and 4 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, preventing any remote agent pod from being scheduled. Because no agent pod could be created, the eval runner never reached the state-polling step, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are absent from the check result.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) is exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. The scheduler reports "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and confirms preemption cannot help. possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: existing remote agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for new probe pods. Preemption is explicitly ruled out by the scheduler message.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. QUATERNARY — Leaked or stuck remote agent pods from prior eval runs consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903), progressively exhausting capacity across runs.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-27T07:32–07:37Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to help. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting runtime evidence, so all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class, and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~129–143 s observed). This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents the eval runner from ever instantiating a remote agent, which in turn causes the complete absence of all required evidence and the eval contract violation. This is an eval-layer signal of a production infrastructure constraint; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader user-facing outage.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is not exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes, the scheduling failure has a different cause (e.g. a quota policy, admission webhook, or pod spec error).

If a subsequent eval run succeeds and collects all 5 required evidence fields without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g. a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained resource exhaustion.
If the pod spec's node affinity/selector is found to be misconfigured and matches 0 nodes rather than 2, the root cause is a configuration error rather than capacity exhaustion.
If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass in a re-run, the failure is isolated to the runtime probe rather than a shared scheduling constraint.

If the cluster has more than 6 nodes or more than 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes at the time of re-run, the earlier failure may have been caused by a temporary node reduction (maintenance, scale-down, or node failure) rather than sustained exhaustion.
